citations.quote:
The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> (Choice function).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.

Let $(X,\mathcal O_X)$ be a ringed space, so $X$ is a topological space and $\mathcal O_X$ is a sheaf of commutative rings. An $\mathcal O_X$-module sheaf $\mathcal F$ is **locally of finite type** if for every $x\in X$ there are an open neighborhood $U$ of $x$, a finite integer $r\ge0$, and sections $s_1,\ldots,s_r\in\mathcal F(U)$ such that their germs generate $\mathcal F_y$ as an $\mathcal O_{X,y}$-module for every $y\in U$.

For an open $V\subseteq X$, a finite integer $p\ge0$, and an $\mathcal O_X$-module morphism $\phi:\mathcal O_V^{\oplus p}\to\mathcal F|_V$, its **relation sheaf** is the kernel sheaf $\ker\phi$. The module sheaf $\mathcal F$ is **coherent** if it is locally of finite type and, for every such $V$, $p$, and $\phi$, the relation sheaf $\ker\phi$ is locally of finite type. Here $\mathcal O_V^{\oplus0}$ is the zero module sheaf.

In particular, for a finite tuple $f_1,\ldots,f_p\in\mathcal O_X(U)$, its holomorphic relation sheaf is the kernel of the morphism $\mathcal O_U^{\oplus p}\to\mathcal O_U$ that sends $(a_1,\ldots,a_p)$ to $\sum_{j=1}^p a_jf_j$. The structure sheaf is coherent when it is coherent as a module over itself. If $M$ is a complex manifold, an **analytic coherent module on $M$** means a coherent module sheaf over its sheaf $\mathcal O_M$ of holomorphic functions.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $M$ be a finite-dimensional complex manifold and let $\mathcal O_M$ be its sheaf of holomorphic functions. For every open $U\subseteq M$ and every finite tuple $f_1,\ldots,f_q\in\mathcal O_M(U)$, the relation sheaf
$$
\ker\!\left(\mathcal O_U^{\oplus q}\longrightarrow\mathcal O_U,\quad(a_1,\ldots,a_q)\longmapsto\sum_{j=1}^q a_jf_j\right)
$$
is locally of finite type: every point has a neighborhood on which one finite family of relation sections generates the relation stalk at every point. Consequently $\mathcal O_M$ is coherent. Coherent $\mathcal O_M$-module sheaves are closed under kernels, cokernels, and finite extensions. For every coherent $\mathcal O_M$-module $\mathcal F$, point $x\in M$, and finite integer $\ell\ge0$, there are a chart neighborhood $W$ of $x$ and finite ranks $p_0,\ldots,p_\ell$ for which
$$
\mathcal O_W^{\oplus p_\ell}\longrightarrow\cdots\longrightarrow\mathcal O_W^{\oplus p_0}\longrightarrow\mathcal F|_W\longrightarrow0
$$
is exact at $\mathcal F|_W$ and at every free term except the leftmost one. No exactness at the leftmost free term and no global analytic free resolution are asserted.

Let $(X,\mathcal O_X)$ be a ringed space and use the coherence definition on the A page. The kernel and cokernel of any morphism between coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module sheaves are coherent. In every short exact sequence $0\to\mathcal F'\to\mathcal E\to\mathcal F''\to0$ of $\mathcal O_X$-module sheaves, if any two of $\mathcal F'$, $\mathcal E$, and $\mathcal F''$ are coherent, then the third is coherent.

Let $\varphi:\mathcal F\to\mathcal G$ be a morphism of sheaves of abelian
groups on a topological space $X$.

The **kernel sheaf** is the subsheaf
$$
\ker(\varphi)\subseteq \mathcal F
$$
defined objectwise by
$$
\ker(\varphi)(U):=\ker\!\bigl(\varphi_U:\mathcal F(U)\to\mathcal G(U)\bigr).
$$

The **cokernel presheaf** is
$$
U\longmapsto \operatorname{coker}\!\bigl(\varphi_U:\mathcal F(U)\to\mathcal G(U)\bigr),
$$
and the **cokernel sheaf** $\operatorname{coker}(\varphi)$ is its
sheafification.

The **image presheaf** is
$$
U\longmapsto \operatorname{im}\!\bigl(\varphi_U:\mathcal F(U)\to\mathcal G(U)\bigr),
$$
and the **image sheaf** $\operatorname{im}(\varphi)$ is its sheafification.

For sheaves of modules on a ringed space, the same formulas are taken in the
corresponding module categories on each open set.

Let
$$
\cdots\longrightarrow \mathcal F_{i-1}\xrightarrow{d_{i-1}}\mathcal F_i\xrightarrow{d_i}\mathcal F_{i+1}\longrightarrow\cdots
$$
be a sequence of sheaves of abelian groups on a topological space $X$. Then the
sequence is exact if and only if, for every point $x\in X$, the stalk sequence
$$
\cdots\longrightarrow (\mathcal F_{i-1})_x\xrightarrow{(d_{i-1})_x}(\mathcal F_i)_x\xrightarrow{(d_i)_x}(\mathcal F_{i+1})_x\longrightarrow\cdots
$$
is exact.

Let $\mathcal F$ be a presheaf on a topological space $X$, and let $x\in X$.

The **neighbourhood category of $x$** is the full subcategory
$$\mathcal N_x\subseteq \operatorname{Open}(X)$$
whose objects are the open neighbourhoods of $x$. Its opposite category is
filtered in the sense of
[[def-filtered-category-and-filtered-colimit]]: it is nonempty because $X$
itself is a neighbourhood of $x$, and for neighbourhoods $U,V$ the
intersection $U\cap V$ is again a neighbourhood of $x$ with arrows
$$U\longrightarrow U\cap V,\qquad V\longrightarrow U\cap V$$
in the opposite category.

Because $\mathcal F$ is contravariant, its restriction to the neighbourhood
category determines a covariant diagram on that opposite category. The
**stalk** of $\mathcal F$ at $x$ is the filtered colimit
$$\mathcal F_x:=\varinjlim_{\mathcal N_x^{\operatorname{op}}}\mathcal F(U).$$

Concretely, $\mathcal F_x$ may be described as equivalence classes of pairs
$(U,s)$ with $U$ an open neighbourhood of $x$ and
$s\in\mathcal F(U)$, where $(U,s)\sim(V,t)$ when $s$ and $t$ agree on some
smaller open neighbourhood of $x$. The next lemma verifies that this is an
equivalence relation.

Fix $m\ge1$, $a\in\mathbb C^m$ and a polyradius $\rho$, let
$f:\Delta_\rho(a)\to\mathbb C$ be continuous and separately holomorphic, let $r$
be a polyradius with $r_k<\rho_k$ for every $k<m$, and let
$C_k(t)=a_k+r_k\exp(it)$ on $[0,2\pi]$. For each multi-index $\alpha$ set

$$c_\alpha:=\frac1{(2\pi i)^m}\int_{C_0}\!\cdots\!\int_{C_{m-1}} f(\zeta)\prod_{k<m}(\zeta_k-a_k)^{-\alpha_k-1}\,d\zeta_{m-1}\cdots d\zeta_0 ,$$

an iterated integral as in the polydisc Cauchy formula. Then, with
$M=\sup_{\Gamma_r(a)}|f|$,

$$|c_\alpha|\le M\prod_{k<m}r_k^{-\alpha_k},$$

and for every real $\theta$ with $0<\theta<1$ the series
$\sum_\alpha c_\alpha(z-a)^\alpha$ converges absolutely and uniformly on
$\overline\Delta_{\theta r}(a)$ with

$$f(z)=\sum_\alpha c_\alpha(z-a)^\alpha\qquad(z\in\overline\Delta_{\theta r}(a)).$$

Since every $z\in\Delta_r(a)$ lies in $\overline\Delta_{\theta r}(a)$ for some
$\theta<1$, the expansion holds throughout $\Delta_r(a)$.

**The coefficients are asserted here only as those iterated integrals.** That
$c_\alpha$ equals $\partial^\alpha f(a)/\alpha!$ needs termwise differentiation
and is not claimed by this statement.

Let $m\ge1$, $a\in\mathbb C^m$ and let $r$ be a polyradius. Suppose
$c,c':\mathbb N^m\to\mathbb C$ both satisfy a bound
$|c_\alpha|\le M\prod_{k<m}r_k^{-\alpha_k}$ and
$|c'_\alpha|\le M'\prod_{k<m}r_k^{-\alpha_k}$, and suppose

$$\sum_\alpha c_\alpha(z-a)^\alpha=\sum_\alpha c'_\alpha(z-a)^\alpha \qquad\text{for every }z\in\Delta_r(a).$$

Then $c_\alpha=c'_\alpha$ for every multi-index $\alpha$. In particular a
function has at most one such power-series representation about a given centre,
and its coefficients are $\partial^\alpha_zf(a)/\alpha!$.

derivations.claim: If $y\in D$ is not the origin, choose an index $k$ with $z_k(y)\ne0$. Then $z_k$ is a unit in the germ ring $\mathcal O_{D,y}$, so the ideal generated by the coordinates is the whole stalk and $\mathcal F_y=0$.

At the origin, evaluation $\operatorname{ev}_0:\mathcal O_{D,0}\to\mathbb C$ is surjective. Its kernel is generated by $z_1,\ldots,z_N$: if $f(0)=0$, its convergent power series has no constant term, and grouping each nonconstant monomial according to the first coordinate with positive exponent writes $f=\sum_i z_i g_i$ with convergent germs $g_i$; each of the finitely many grouped subseries remains convergent on a smaller polydisc. Conversely every such sum vanishes at $0$. Hence $\mathcal F_0\cong\mathbb C$.

At a point $y\ne0$, choose $k$ with $z_k(y)\ne0$. If $a=(a_1,\ldots,a_N)$ is a relation germ in the stalk from [F6], then $a_k=-\sum_{i\ne k}a_i z_i/z_k$, so
$$
a=\sum_{i\ne k}(a_i/z_k)(z_ke_i-z_ie_k).
$$
Each vector $z_ke_i-z_ie_k$ is one of the stated pairwise sections or its negative. Thus those sections generate the relation stalk at every nonzero point, including when $N=1$, where the sum is empty.

Let $a=(a_1,\ldots,a_N)$ be a relation germ at the origin, so $\sum_i a_i z_i=0$. We prove by induction on $N$ that it is generated by the stated pairwise sections. For $N=1$, $a_1z_1=0$ and the germ ring is a domain by [F5], so $a_1=0$. For $N>1$, restrict to $z_N=0$; the first $N-1$ coefficients form a relation among $z_1,\ldots,z_{N-1}$. By induction subtract a combination of the pairwise sections with both indices below $N$, extending their coefficient germs independently of $z_N$. The resulting first $N-1$ coefficients vanish at $z_N=0$.

By [F5], each remaining coefficient has a convergent series divisible by $z_N$, so write $a_i=z_Nc_i$ for $i<N$. The relation becomes $z_N(\sum_{i<N}c_i z_i+a_N)=0$. Since the germ ring is a domain, $a_N=-\sum_{i<N}c_i z_i$, and the remaining vector is $\sum_{i<N}c_i(z_Ne_i-z_i e_N)$, a combination of the stated pairwise sections.

At every point, steps 2.1–2.3 show that the pairwise sections generate the kernel stalk. Therefore [F4] identifies their generated subsheaf with $\ker\mu$. The quotient sequence is exact by the definition of $\mathcal F$ as a cokernel.

Under the assumed Axiom of Choice [A1], [F2] makes $\mathcal O_D$ coherent. Repeatedly applying the finite-extension case of [F3] to the split sequences $0\to\mathcal O_D^{\oplus(j-1)}\to\mathcal O_D^{\oplus j}\to\mathcal O_D\to0$ shows that $\mathcal O_D^{\oplus N}$ is coherent. The cokernel case of [F3] applied to $\mu$ then makes $\mathcal F$ coherent.

boundaries.evidence: The hypothesis N≥1 excludes an empty coordinate family, and the boundary case N=1 with empty syzygy family is proved in steps 2.1–2.3.
The quotient stalk is computed as zero off the origin and C at the origin in steps 1.1–1.2.
For N=1 the relation kernel is zero and the pairwise generating family is empty, as shown in steps 2.1–2.3.
